description: Broker Deployed as a Single Instance
rationale: A single-instance broker runs on one instance in one Availability Zone with nothing to take over from it, so a maintenance window, a reboot, an instance failure or the loss of that Availability Zone stops it, and the messages it has not delivered stay in its storage until it comes back. Everything the broker sits between stops with it: producers that cannot hand a message over either drop it or hold it in memory until they fail too, which is how a queue meant to absorb a failure becomes the failure. An active/standby pair on ActiveMQ, or a cluster deployment on RabbitMQ, keeps the queue reachable across the maintenance Amazon MQ performs on the account's behalf as well as across an Availability Zone failure.
remediation: Recreate the broker in a multi-Availability-Zone deployment, as the deployment mode cannot be changed after creation: active/standby for ActiveMQ, cluster for RabbitMQ
